feed.title: Meta reaches $17B settlement over social media addiction claims

While Meta denies the allegations, the agreement requires court approval and addresses state-law and federal COPPA claims, though it does not fully resolve broader multidistrict litigation from personal injury plaintiffs or school districts.

Critics argue this practice gives preferential access to critical government information, potentially violating the First and Fifth Amendments, and differs from other news services because the information originates directly from a former president who stands to profit. A federal lawsuit has been filed, and congressional Democrats are proposing legislation to block such pay-for-access schemes for government employees' communications.
